references.text: God renews the promise to Abraham with Isaac and confirms the covenant with Abraham's descendants.
God renews the promise to Abraham with Jacob and confirms the covenant with Abraham's descendants.
God specifies that the covenant shall continue through Isaac as an everlasting covenant for his descendants.
God heard Israel's cry of distress and remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The psalmist praises God who remembers His eternal covenant with Abraham, confirmed as a statute for Israel.
Zechariah praises God who remembers His holy covenant, the oath He swore to Abraham.
Paul explains that the promises were given to Abraham and his offspring, and that the covenant was ratified by God.
God's promise to Abraham is used as an example of God's unchangeable purpose and pledge.
Abraham's faith and God's promises to him are highlighted as examples of faith.
Paul explains that not all of Abraham's physical descendants are his true children, but the children of the promise are counted as his offspring.
Both establish an eternal covenant extending to all generations, but with different scope (Abraham's offspring versus all living things).
Prophetic restoration of the eternal covenant relationship ('I am your God, you are my people') promised to Abraham.
Direct reference to restoring the original covenant from Abraham's time as an everlasting covenant.
Identical language regarding the covenant with 'you and your descendants' emphasizing continuity in God's plan.
Direct confirmation and continuation of Abraham's covenant promises concerning numerous descendants and land to Isaac.
Prophetic expansion of the eternal covenant, focusing on God's eternal presence among His people.
Confirms that God's faithfulness to the 'covenant with the fathers' (Abraham) is the basis for being their God.
Operationalization of the Abrahamic covenant relationship ('I am your God') in the Mosaic law.
The new covenant is presented as the final fulfillment of Abraham's eternal covenant relationship.
Uses Abraham's covenant language of 'generation to generation' to describe David's dynasty as part of God's eternal plan.
Prophetic restoration of the perfect covenant relationship ('I am your God') promised to Abraham.
Restoration of the central covenant formula ('I am your God') that characterizes Abraham's covenant.
Confirms the unshakable nature of the 'eternal covenant' promised to Abraham, where God never turns away.
Links the Davidic covenant to the Abrahamic 'eternal covenant' as a messianic promise.
Prophetic confirmation that the land promise in Abraham's eternal covenant will be fulfilled forever.
A parallel in the concept of an eternal covenant with a man and his descendants, but with different theological focus (universal vs. specific).
Prophetic restoration of the perfect covenant relationship ('I am your God') promised to Abraham.
Direct confirmation and continuation of Abraham's covenant promises of numerous descendants and an eternal land to Jacob.
The Exodus from Egypt is presented as a fulfillment of Abraham's covenant promise to be their God.
Confirms that the inheritance of the land is a fulfillment of God's oath to the fathers (Abraham) in the eternal covenant.
The new covenant is presented as the inner renewal of Abraham's eternal covenant relationship.
Uses the marriage metaphor to describe the 'eternal covenant' and God's unshakable faithfulness to Israel.
Prophetic restoration of the covenant relationship ('I am your God') through a transformed heart.
Confirms that God's blessing and fruitfulness in the law is a continuation of Abraham's covenant promises.
